skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Run Tavily and Exa web search, answer, and extraction tasks through the inference.sh CLI for research and source gathering.
skill.summary: Search the web and extract page content through Tavily and Exa using inference.sh.

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and example code fences. The meaningful risks are the broad Bash(infsh *) permission, external search and extraction data transfer, and minor remote content dependencies.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed commands to the specific infsh app run calls this skill needs, or require explicit user confirmation before running other infsh subcommands.

remediation.issue: Sensitive data can be sent to external providers
remediation.suggestion: Document that queries, URLs, page content, and prompts may be processed by inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter. Warn users not to submit secrets.

remediation.issue: Remote image and install links depend on external hosts
remediation.suggestion: Use marketplace-hosted media when possible and pin trusted installation documentation with integrity guidance.

content.value_statement: Current research needs recent sources and clean page text. This skill routes searches and extraction through Tavily and Exa using inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Run Tavily search assistant queries through the inference.sh CLI.
Extract clean text and images from one or more web pages.
Run Exa search for relevant links with context.
Request direct factual answers from Exa.
Chain search or extraction output into LLM summarization workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account.
Search quality depends on Tavily, Exa, and accessible public web content.
External providers may process submitted queries, URLs, and extracted text.
Does not replace source verification for high-stakes decisions.

use_cases.title: Research Briefs
use_cases.description: Collect recent sources, extract relevant pages, and summarize findings for a focused brief.

use_cases.title: RAG Source Gathering
use_cases.description: Find and extract web pages that can seed retrieval datasets or knowledge bases.

use_cases.title: Fact Checking
use_cases.description: Search for source material and compare direct answers against cited pages.

prompt_templates.title: Find Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use web-search to find recent sources on [topic]. Return a short answer with source links and publication context.

prompt_templates.title: Extract A Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use web-search to extract the main content from [URL]. Summarize the key points and note any missing access.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Tavily and Exa for [topic]. Compare the strongest sources, their dates, and their main claims.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Research Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic], extract the best pages, then prepare a structured research brief with citations and uncertainty notes.

output_examples.input: Find current sources about agent memory systems.
output_examples.output: A concise source list with titles, links, dates, short summaries, and a note on which sources look most authoritative.

output_examples.input: Extract and summarize a long article about search ranking.
output_examples.output: A short summary of the article, the main arguments, notable images, and any extraction limits reported by the provider.

output_examples.input: Compare Tavily and Exa results for a technical topic.
output_examples.output: A comparison of overlapping sources, unique sources, answer quality, and follow-up searches to improve coverage.

best_practices: Use specific queries with date, location, and source-quality requirements when needed.
Review source links before using extracted text in final work.
Avoid sending secrets, private documents, or restricted URLs to external providers.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated answers as verified facts without checking sources.
Do not extract private or paywalled content unless you have permission.
Do not use broad searches when a precise query would reduce noise.

faq.question: What services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses inference.sh CLI apps for Tavily search, Tavily extraction, Exa search, Exa answers, and Exa extraction.

faq.question: Does it require setup?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the inference.sh CLI installed and an authenticated inference.sh account.

faq.question: Can it browse any website?
faq.answer: It can request public web content that the providers can access. Some sites may block extraction or require permission.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is submitted content private?
faq.answer: Submitted queries, URLs, and extracted content may be processed by external services. Do not send secrets or restricted data.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect source lists, direct answers, extracted text, images, and summaries depending on the selected app.
